Environment: clouds, fog, rain and lightning in Doppio

Stable Doppio Last updated: 2026-11-21

Clouds that shade the ground, height fog, rain with depth, wind and lightning with thunder as one system that agrees with the sun and with Photon's GI, and the Environment tab that manages it.

The scene's weather lives in two reflected components on one entity: Volumetric Clouds (the sky) and Weather (fog, rain, wind, lightning and the coupling between everything). Doppio edits them from the Environment tab (View menu, next to Photon) and from the Inspector: both write the same fields, so they never disagree, and scripts and agents use the same fields too.

1. What was already there#

The environment work reused what the engine had instead of building a second copy:

Part Before Now
Clouds VolumetricCloudsComponent drawn by sky.frag (ray-marched, procedural, with wind and mist), serialised but not reflected and with no UI Reflected, editable in the tab; new fields Tint, Darkness and Sky Light appended
Fog A linear post-process fog (deferredFog) and the forward pass's volumetric light Both stay as they are; a new exponential height fog in the composite pass, with the sky fading into it
Wetness modWetness per mesh renderer A scene-wide wetness added on top of it
Rain Nothing Layered screen-space streaks and wet surfaces
Photon sky A fixed sky colour times Sky intensity The same colour times a weather factor (section 6)

2. The Environment tab#

The tab edits the first entity that carries the weather components. Add environment creates one on a new entity (clouds on, from the Clear sky preset) when the scene has none. Every edit goes through the engine's component API and records one undo step (a slider is one step per field, not per value); a preset is one step.

The hierarchy's + palette (World) also has an Environment entry: it creates the environment entity once and, when the scene already has one, selects it and opens this tab, so there is never a second one.

Control Field What it does
Preset Off, Clear sky, Cloudy, Fog, Light rain or Storm: sets clouds, fog and rain together
Clouds Volumetric Clouds Section 3
Fog Weather Section 4
Rain Weather Section 5
Sky, sun and light Weather Enabled (master switch) and Link Sky (section 6)

3. Clouds#

Procedural volumetric clouds between two altitudes, ray-marched in the sky pass, so they cost nothing when the sky is hidden.

Control Field What it does
Enabled, Quality Enabled, Quality Off, Low (8 steps), Medium (16) or High (24)
Coverage Coverage 0 is a clear sky, 1 a full one
Density Density Extinction: thin and wispy to thick
Base altitude, Top altitude Base Altitude, Top Altitude The layer's bounds, in metres
Detail Detail Weight of the high-frequency octaves
Wind speed, Wind dir Wind Speed, Wind Direction Drift, in metres per second and degrees around +Y
Sun scatter Sun Scatter How strongly the sun lights them
Darkness Darkness 0 to 1: darker, heavier clouds for a storm
Sky light Sky Light The light that fills the shadowed side
Mist, Mist height Mist Density, Mist Height Ground mist at the horizon (above 0 it also switches on the forward pass's volumetric fog, a few milliseconds at 720p: the presets leave it at 0)
Sun-lit tint Tint Colour multiplied into the sun-lit side: orange at dusk, grey in a storm
Clouds dim the sun Cast Shadows The cloud cover lowers the direct light (section 8)
Shadows on the ground, Shadow strength Ground Shadows, Shadow Strength Moving cloud shadows on everything the sun lights, and in Photon's bounce (section 8)
Silver lining Silver Lining A bright rim on thin cloud edges in front of the sun
Sun shafts Sun Shafts Rays through the gaps of the clouds while the sun is in view

The clouds animate with the wind whenever the sky is drawn.

4. Fog#

Exponential height fog, integrated along each view ray in the composite pass: density * exp(-falloff * (y - baseHeight)) per metre. Because it uses the depth buffer it covers every object, terrain and water alike, and the sky fades into it near the horizon.

Control Field What it does
Fog Fog Enabled The switch
Density Fog Density Per metre at the base height
Falloff Fog Height Falloff How fast it thins with height; 0 is uniform
Base height Fog Base Height World height where the density applies
Start Fog Start Metres before the fog begins
Max opacity Fog Max Opacity The most it can hide
Sky blend Fog Sky Blend 0 uses the fog colour, 1 uses the sky's own colour at the horizon in the direction looked at
Sun glow, Glow tight Fog Sun Scatter, Fog Sun Exponent The glow of the fog towards the sun
Fog colour Fog Color sRGB

With a sky blend above 0 the fog samples the same sky texture the sky pass draws, so a ground haze matches the horizon behind it.

5. Rain#

Rain is still one screen-space shader, with no particles and no models, but it is computed in the world: six shells of falling streaks from 2.5 m to about 60 m in front of the camera, each a lattice of cells in world space. A streak is a slanted capsule with a bright head, it is hidden wherever geometry is nearer than its shell, and a drop near the camera is long and sharp while a far one is short and soft. Because the shells live in the world, moving the camera gives parallax: the near drops sweep past and the far ones hang, which is what gives the rain its depth.

Control Field What it does
Rain Rain Enabled The switch
Intensity Rain Intensity 0 to 1: how many streaks, and how much the scene loses contrast
Wind speed, Wind dir Rain Wind Speed, Rain Wind Direction The wind's velocity: the whole lattice leans along it against a fall speed of about 9 m/s
Drop length Rain Drop Length 0 to 1
Fall speed Rain Speed Animation speed
Brightness Rain Brightness How bright a streak is; the colour follows the sky and the light level
Wetness Rain Wetness How wet surfaces get at full intensity
Splashes Rain Splashes 0 to 1: rings and sparks where the rain meets an upward-facing surface within about 35 m (the normal is rebuilt from the depth buffer, so it also works on the terrain)

Wet surfaces: the scene-wide wetness is intensity * wetness and is added to each mesh renderer's own Wetness. The lit shader darkens the albedo and makes the surface glossy, as it already did for modWetness.

6. Wind#

One wind drives the whole scene. Its mean is Rain Wind Speed and Rain Wind Direction (the clouds keep their own drift), and it surges: a sum of slow sines, never negative and never repeating within minutes, scaled by Gusts (Wind Gust, 0 to 1). The same gust factor leans the rain, shakes the foliage and is reported by the engine, so everything moves together.

Control Field What it does
Gusts Wind Gust 0 is a steady wind, 1 surges between calm and about twice the mean
Foliage sway Wind Foliage Multiplies the sway of foliage materials by 1 + value * speed / 8 * gust; 0 leaves foliage alone
Weather sound, Volume Audio Enabled, Audio Volume Plays the rain, the wind and the thunder (section 7); a preset leaves them as you set them

7. Lightning and thunder#

Switch Lightning on and the sky strikes on its own. Strikes are deterministic: each minute is cut into slots and every slot holds one strike whose moment, bearing, distance and strength are hashed from the seed, so the same seed gives the same storm and a test can predict it. With the link on, lightning needs an overcast sky (cloud cover or rain of at least 0.4), as there is no lightning in a clear sky.

What a strike does, all within a second:

  • The flash. Up to three return strokes flicker, over an afterglow of the cloud. The flash lights the scene as a cold directional light from where the bolt struck (no shadow of its own), so it also reaches Photon: the bounce flashes with it. It raises the sky light and Photon's sky, flares the rain and lights the fog and the clouds from inside.
  • The bolt. A forked line from the cloud base to the horizon, in the sky pass, at the strike's bearing.
  • The thunder. Each strike raises one event that arrives after the sound's travel time (distance / 343 m/s). Doppio logs it in the Console (Thunder, 1.2 km away); the engine makes no sound itself, see the limits.
Control Field What it does
Lightning Lightning Enabled The switch
Thunder events Thunder Whether strikes raise thunder events
Strikes / min Lightning Rate One strike per slot of 60 / rate seconds
Flash Lightning Intensity 0 to 2: the brightness of the flash
Nearest, Farthest Lightning Distance Min, Lightning Distance Max Where strikes land, in metres; a close strike is brighter and louder

Thunder is also heard: with Audio Enabled on (the Sound card), the session plays each clap from noise, panned to the strike's bearing and quieter with the distance, along with a rain bed and a wind bed that follow the weather (see the audio system). Off by default, so a scene stays silent until it asks. A game or a script that wants its own sound can still poll caffeine_session_poll_thunder (section 12).

8. How they agree: sun, sky and Photon#

With Link sky, sun and fog on (the default) the sections act on each other, and on the light:

When Then
It rains and clouds are on Coverage rises to at least 0.55 + 0.40 * intensity, the density grows by up to 80% and the clouds darken
It rains and fog is on The fog density grows by 1 + intensity
The sky is overcast (cloud cover, or rain) The sun's intensity drops by up to 80% for every stage that uses it: the forward shader, the cloud lighting, the fog glow and Photon's injection
The sky is overcast The sky light Photon falls back to, and the forward ambient, grow by up to 25% and tend to a neutral grey of the same brightness
Thick fog The sky light takes the fog's hue, keeping its brightness

Photon needs nothing new for these: the sun reaches it through the same light list, and its sky radiance is the fixed sky colour times Sky intensity, now also times the weather's scale and tint (kPhotonSkyRadiance). These factors depend only on the settings, never on time or on the frame, so they add no noise: Photon's temporal average and its per-probe sampling offsets keep working as before, and the fog is applied after Photon's resolve, so it also softens what is left of the noise in the distance.

With the link off every section acts alone, and the clouds keep exactly the values in the component.

Clouds that move the light#

Three effects tie the clouds to the lighting without baking anything (switch them on in Clouds; the presets do):

  • Shadows on the ground (Ground Shadows, Shadow Strength). The forward shaders trace the sun's ray to the cloud layer and read the same noise as the sky at two heights of it, so a cloud's shadow crosses the ground, the terrain and every object the sun lights, moves with the wind and agrees with what the sky shows. Photon's injection reads the same function for every voxel, so the bounce follows the shadow (the near field already did: it reads the forward pass's direct light). No texture is added: the forward pass is at the 16-sampler limit.
  • Silver lining (Silver Lining). The thin edges of the clouds in front of the sun glow, by forward scattering.
  • Sun shafts (Sun Shafts). A screen-space radial gather towards the sun: rays through the gaps of the clouds, in 14 steps, and only while the sun is in front of the camera (looking away costs nothing).

9. Presets#

Preset Clouds Fog Rain
Off off off off
Clear sky coverage 0.25 off off
Cloudy coverage 0.75, a little dark off off
Fog coverage 0.55 density 0.03, falloff 0.035, sky blend 0.7 off
Light rain coverage 0.8 thin intensity 0.35
Storm coverage 0.95, dark, fast wind, gusts 0.7, lightning 9 a minute thin, grey intensity 0.95, strong wind

Every preset with clouds also switches on ground shadows, a silver lining, a little sun shaft strength and foliage sway.

10. Components, scripts and agents#

The two components are reflected, so add_component and set_component_field by name reach every field (the Inspector shows them too). The Weather struct is serialised as a raw prefix and a scene without it renders exactly as before; the new cloud fields are appended, so an older scene keeps their defaults (no tint, no darkness).

Agents (ICED_MCP=1, feature agent) read the environment query and use show_environment, environment_add, environment_set and environment_preset:

json
{ "action": "environment_preset", "args": { "name": "Storm" } }
{ "action": "environment_set", "args": { "field": "fog_density", "value": 0.02 } }
{ "action": "environment_set", "args": { "field": "fog_color", "value": [0.5, 0.55, 0.6] } }

11. Limits#

  • Rain is a screen-space effect with world-space depth: no particles and no collision, and it does not know about roofs (a streak is hidden by geometry in front of it, but rain falls on the camera inside a building too). Splashes reach about 35 m and only on surfaces the depth buffer shows.
  • The wetness is not smoothed in time, and it does not reach terrain, which has its own shader.
  • Fog and rain are drawn in the final pass, so they are not in the images reflection probes and planar reflections show.
  • Cloud shadows are traced at two heights of the layer with a soft three-octave noise: they are soft shadows, not sharp edges, and they do not shade the sky light. Photon's voxels read the same function, so the bounce is as soft.
  • The weather's sound plays in the editor session (and wherever a session is hosted), not in caffeine-runtime, which does not use this renderer. It is mono and made from noise: it does not follow rooms or roofs (the rain is as loud indoors), and the thunder is panned but has no Doppler or echo.
  • The bolt is a sky effect: it has no geometry, casts no shadow and strikes nothing.
  • Rain with the link on thickens existing clouds; with no clouds component the sky stays as it is.

12. Where it lives and how it is tested#

Part Where
Components src/caffeine/ecs/WeatherComponents.hpp (Weather, serialised as scene type 60), include/caffeine/environment/VolumetricClouds.hpp; both reflected through scripts/gen-component-reflection.py (ids 128 and 129)
The coupling src/caffeine/scene/WeatherSystem.hpp: resolveWeather() is pure, so every rule in section 8 is a unit test; the wind gust and the lightning (windGustFactor, lightningStrike, lightningAt, thunderBetween) are pure functions too
Renderer GpuSceneRenderer (resolves the weather once per frame, scales the lights, the ambient and Photon's sky), sky.frag (clouds, bolt, silver lining), scene_lit.frag and terrain_lit.frag (cloud shadows), photon_inject.comp (the same shadow for the bounce), post_composite.frag (fog, rain, sun shafts)
Panel uikit/panels/environment.rs (one table of switches, numbers and colours drives the panel, the presets and the agent), windows/main/environment.rs

The weather itself goes through the reflected components. C ABI v19 adds two read-only calls for what moves on its own: caffeine_session_weather_state (the flash, the bolt, the wind's gust, the clock of the strikes) and caffeine_session_poll_thunder (the claps that have arrived since the last call), plus caffeine_session_audio_state for the weather's sound (device, levels, claps).

Nothing of this moves while the editor is stopped. C ABI v21 adds caffeine_session_set_simulating: off, a rendered frame stands still (clouds, rain, wind on foliage, lightning, water and the scene's sound do not advance and the sound device closes); on, each frame advances them. A new session simulates, so the runtime and older callers are unchanged; Doppio turns it off at start and on only while Play is active, and a stopped viewport draws a frame only when something changed (an edit, the camera, a setting), a few more while TAA and Photon settle, and none otherwise.

Tests:

  • tests/test_weather.cpp: defaults, the coupling rules, scene round trip and old-prefix loading, reflection, the gust, the strikes (the same seed gives the same storm, the flash peaks and fades, thunder arrives at distance / 343 s) and the thunder synth.
  • tests/test_weather_gpu.cpp: the real post stack on a known scene (needs a GPU, skipped without one): fog hides the far half and not the near half, the start distance and the maximum opacity, rain adds streaks on the sky and none behind near geometry, a flash lights the rain and the fog, wind bends the streaks, a floor gets splashes, and shafts stream from an HDR sun only while it is ahead.
  • windows/main/tests.rs, module environment_weather: the panel's table, the presets through the engine, undo, and images of a road of blocks: everything off equals no weather, fog loses contrast with distance, rain adds streaks that fall, wet roads darken, clouds and their tint show in the sky, an overcast sky dims the sun only when linked, Photon's sky light greys without adding flicker, cloud shadows darken the lit ground only while on, wind changes the rain, and a storm flashes the scene and raises thunder once the sound has travelled (and nothing with the lightning off).
  • UI flows environment-panel.json and environment-scene.json, and the capture flow captures/flows/capture-environment-docs.json (run it with scripts/capture-environment-docs.sh, which also writes the renders this page shows).

Things to know when you write a test like these:

  • The renderer is not bit-exact between still frames (ambient occlusion and dithering): two frames of one scene differ by about 0.03 levels on average and by up to about 10 at single pixels. "Nothing changes" is therefore measured against that noise, not with equality.
  • A linked fog also hands its hue to the sky light, even when its maximum opacity is 0: switch the link off to compare a fog that hides nothing with no fog.
  • Mist Density also drives the forward pass's volumetric fog, so set it to 0 when a test isolates the sun.
  • Compare images with a difference helper, not with assert_eq! on the pixels: a failure prints every byte.
